title: Event-driven GUIs with Tkinter

spans.text: Tkinter is Python's standard-library interface for desktop graphical applications. Widgets such as Label, Entry, and Button are arranged with geometry managers; callbacks handle clicks and keyboard events, while mainloop waits for window events. Unlike a terminal script, the application remains active until the window closes.

spans.code:
import tkinter as tk

root = tk.Tk()
message = tk.StringVar(value='Hazır')
label = tk.Label(root, textvariable=message)
label.pack(padx=12, pady=8)
tk.Button(root, text='Hello', command=lambda: message.set('Hello!')).pack()
root.mainloop()
A window opens with a button; clicking it changes the label to Hello!.

spans.text: Button's command connects a click to a function, and mainloop keeps the window responsive.

spans.title: Important tip
spans.text: Keep callbacks short: long work can block the event loop and freeze the window.

spans.title: Warning
spans.text: Never execute user-entered text with eval/exec; GUI input is untrusted.
